topic: Spring Boot and REST API Development
learningObjectives: Explain the structure of a Spring Boot REST application.
Design REST endpoints using controllers and HTTP methods.
Construct a basic request-to-response flow for a Spring Boot API.

activities.title: Spring Boot REST Architecture
activities.instruction: Explore the main layers of a Spring Boot REST application.

content.concept: A typical Spring Boot REST application separates HTTP request handling, business logic, data access, and persistence responsibilities so each layer has a focused role.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: REST Endpoint Anatomy
activities.instruction: Explore the important parts of a REST endpoint.

content.concept: A REST endpoint combines an HTTP method and URL path with request data, controller handling, and an HTTP response.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Defines the operation, such as GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE.
Identifies the API resource being accessed.
Contains data sent by the client when the operation requires a payload.
Java method that handles the mapped request.
Contains the resulting status, headers, and optional response body.

activities.title: Choose the REST Method
activities.instruction: Choose the HTTP method that best matches the requested operation.

content.concept: REST APIs commonly use GET to retrieve resources, POST to create resources, PUT or PATCH to update resources, and DELETE to remove resources.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Request-to-Response Builder
activities.instruction: Build the flow of a request through a Spring Boot REST API.

content.concept: A typical Spring Boot API flow starts with an HTTP request, reaches a controller, invokes service logic, accesses data when necessary, and returns an HTTP response.
